A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SciRIFF dataset and SciTulu models. All 28 pages of each version, including figures, tables and Appendices A–D, support comparison. The appendix pages with unextractable text were inspected visually.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations and training ablations in Tables 3–4 and Figure 3, with detailed task results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports a qualitative finding from preliminary comparisons of LLM judges in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Dataset construction, instruction templates, structured outputs and the SciTulu finetuning procedure remain unchanged. Both versions adapt Tulu V2 using a mixture of scientific and general instructions.

E1.justification: The 54-task collection, nine held-out science tasks and general evaluations are retained. Table 1 adds task-category labels, but the corresponding inputs, outputs and appendix examples establish no change in actual task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains Tulu V2, Llama 2 7B Chat, Llama 3 8B Instruct, GPT-3.5 Turbo and GPT-4 as comparators. The checkpoint/data comparisons in the ablations are also unchanged. Alternative LLM judges are evaluation checks, not new SciTulu baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix D newly documents an auxiliary check using GPT-4 and Claude-2 as alternatives to GPT-3.5 for judging outputs. The primary GPT-3.5 judging protocol, metrics, training budgets and model sizes remain unchanged; no rerun of the main evaluations is established.

E4.justification: v3 adds a brief judge-sensitivity finding: preliminary results were reportedly similar across GPT-3.5 and alternative proprietary judges. No quantitative analysis accompanies it. The existing checkpoint, data-mixture and training-sample ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests for the model comparisons. v3's preliminary judge discussion adds no run counts, seeds or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The numerical benchmark and ablation results are unchanged, including Tables 3–4, Tables 6–7 and Figure 3. Appendix D adds the qualitative finding that GPT-3.5 judging produced results similar to GPT-4 and Claude-2, without reporting comparison scores.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. Task definitions and metric descriptions are retained; the new negative-transfer discussion introduces no mathematical assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain the 137K-example, 54-task resource and sample-efficient scientific adaptation of instruction-following models. The abstract and introduction retain the claimed 28.1% and 6.5% science improvements at 7B and 70B.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds negative task transfer as a possible explanation for uneven benefits and recommends task-selection ablations. Section 6 explicitly discusses concentration in AI and biomedical/clinical domains. Appendix D adds cost and efficiency as the rationale for choosing GPT-3.5.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters and hardware in Appendix B, truncation instructions in Appendix A.3, task prompts and metric descriptions, and code/data/checkpoint access information are retained. The added judge discussion supplies no additional implementation instructions or reproducible details for its preliminary check.

R1.justification: v3 adds Jang et al. (2023) and Asai et al. (2022) to support the negative-transfer discussion. The broader related-work account and positioning of SciRIFF relative to existing instruction datasets remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized discussion additions, task-category terminology, an acknowledgements section and replacement of the conference footer with 'Preprint. Under review.' Most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 adds category labels and adjusts column layout; its new SciERC relation-extraction label conflicts with the retained entity-recognition description. Table 3 corrects boldface highlighting for Llama 3's MultiCite and MuP scores. Figure 1 is visually restyled without changing its examples.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves interpretation by explicitly discussing domain imbalance and possible negative transfer, and improves accuracy of presentation through corrected Table 3 highlighting. These benefits are limited: the new judge check is unquantified, and Table 1 introduces an erroneous SciERC category label. The main empirical evidence remains unchanged, so the overall gain is small.
